content.comment_body: I have a very basic question that I can't seem to find the answer to online. I recently purchased a house that has all [product_name] modules installed. I also bought the [product_name] software and connected the [product_name] to my laptop. However, I'm having trouble transferring information from the [product_name] to my laptop. It seems like I'm missing a simple step, but I can't find clear instructions online. Thanks in advance.

Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum. Could you please specify the following details: - Which [product_name] software version are you using? - What type of [product_name] module do you have (please provide the exact [article_no])? - What are the IP address and subnet mask settings for your [product_name]? - What are the IP address and subnet mask settings for your PC or laptop? - Is your PC or laptop connected directly to the [product_name]?

Thanks for your response. I realize I should've provided more details initially. I have three [product_name] units ([article_no]) and one power module ([article_no]). All three are connected to a switch, so I can use ethernet to access each unit individually; the network link works without issue. The [product_name] software version is [version_no]. I know that at least one of the units was programmed with a timer circuit. My question is: how do I transfer the diagrams to my laptop? Do I need to stop the unit from running before I can retrieve this information?

I realize now that I misunderstood your initial question. I thought you were unable to connect to the [product_name] units. It seems you already have a successful connection. If you want to download programs from the [product_name] units to your laptop, it can only be done when the units are stopped. It appears you already knew this. What specific information do you still need help with?
I've attached a video that demonstrates how to download a program from a [product_name] module to your computer.

If your [product_name] module has a display and keypad, you can try checking its IP address and then adjust your PC’s IP address to ensure it’s within the same subnet. If the program is password protected, you’ll need to obtain the password from the previous owner.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are finding it difficult to locate straightforward instructions for extracting program data from [product_name] controllers to their laptops. There is uncertainty about whether program diagrams can be retrieved while the devices are still operational, leading to confusion and hesitation during the download process.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for clear and simple step-by-step guidance on downloading or accessing current program circuits from [product_name] controllers to their laptops using [product_name] software, preferably without interrupting normal operation.
